ctx.x: now. Where are we? We were in Pittsburgh. (inaudible). How about Linton Garner?

I didn't know Linton. I met Linton in later years when Linton was an accompanist for Timmy Rogers. Linton was a very good pianist also, but I didn't -- Billy Strayhorn used to talk about Linton because they were friends.

items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: Duke and Billy had such a great rapport, musically and otherwise... I don't think I'll ever have any experiences like that again in life. Because I enjoyed just being there.

ctx.x: But any way, that was one of the things. And used to have such a marvelous time. Duke and Stray Horn before the show -- see, we'd do the show at night, but during the day Duke and Stray Horn would go to the auditorium and they would just play, see. It was interchangeable. He just had this pianist, two pianists here, and they would just play it. So Jimmie Jones and I would always be there, and listen, and some great things were happening. Duke and Billy had such a great rapport, musically and otherwise, you know,…
As a matter of fact I'm going to do one of the tunes of Billy Stray Horn for his next album that I'm doing to

do, Strange Feeling. And nobody has ever done it. I -- are you aware of this tune? It's a beautiful tune. So Jimmy Jones was over my house a few days ago, and I said, Jimmie, look, here's a tune that I'm going to do. He said, oh, yeah, I know that tune. I said, yeah, have you heard this recording here, that Stray Horn did as piano and voices. Do you have this "Peaceful" side of Billy Stray Horn. Oh yes, I have it.
